subject: CAIQ control decomposition and evidence sources request
messages:
From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@zephyrcloud.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ZephyrCloud Security <security@zephyrcloud.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: CAIQ control decomposition + evidence sources

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this on. ZephyrCloud is kicking off a vendor CAIQ review and we need a concise mapping that does two things:

- Decompose each CSA/CAIQ control into the specific Redwood runtime artifacts we can provide (e.g., runtime logs, KV cache control, deployment manifests, access control rosters, HSM audit notes).
- Identify the primary evidence artifact for each control and a secondary fallback artifact if the primary is scoped (e.g., aggregated logs vs. sample session logs).

Deliverables we need: a CSV-style mapping (control ID -> artifact -> owner -> retention window) and a short owner roster showing who will produce/provide each artifact. Goal: initial package by next Thursday (2027-07-08).

Attached: Zephyr-CAIQ-questionnaire-v1.pdf (their list of prioritized controls). Priority for them: identity & access, key management, and runtime telemetry for inference requests.

A couple of clarifying items before we lock a plan:
- Do you have a suggested template for the mapping CSV?
- Are there any PII/production logs we can only provide as samples or redacted extracts?

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow to kick off.

Thanks,
Alex Morales
Security Engineer, ZephyrCloud
alex.morales@zephyrcloud.com

---
Attachments: Zephyr-CAIQ-questionnaire-v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@zephyrcloud.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ control decomposition + evidence sources

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask and the priorities. We can deliver the CSV mapping + owner roster on the timeline you suggested. High-level plan below; see attached plan doc for the sprint breakdown.

Plan (summary):
- Day 0–1: Triage the provided questionnaire and tag priority controls (we'll use your identity, KMS, telemetry buckets).
- Day 2–4: Populate control -> evidence mapping. For each control we will provide: primary artifact, fallback artifact, artifact owner (internal), typical retention period, and any redaction/scoping notes.
- Day 5: Internal QA and redact PII from any logs; prepare sample artifacts and a README describing how to validate them.
- Delivery: CSV + owner roster + a small bucket of sample artifacts (redacted logs, runbook excerpts).

Template: attached "RDW-CAIQ-decomposition-plan-v0.1.pdf" includes a proposed CSV schema and an "owner-roster-template.csv" we will populate. Priyom will lead artifact collection; Karthik will validate KMS/HSM claims and provide the HSM attestation snippets.

Quick asks for you to confirm:
1) Is Zephyr comfortable with redacted session logs (timestamp + request-id + anonymized client id) rather than full payloads?
2) Do you require chain-of-custody for any of the artifacts (signed attestations preferred)?

If yes to (2), we can add a short attestation from our security team and include DocuSign if required. I can set up a 30-minute slot tomorrow 10:30–11:00 PT if that works for you.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Attachments: RDW-CAIQ-decomposition-plan-v0.1.pdf (pdf, 480KB)

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ control decomposition + evidence sources

Alex / Soojin — looping in details and an initial artifacts index. See below and attached templates.

Quoted from Soojin: 
> Template: attached "RDW-CAIQ-decomposition-plan-v0.1.pdf" includes a proposed CSV schema and an "owner-roster-template.csv" we will populate. Priyom will lead artifact collection; Karthik will validate KMS/HSM claims and provide the HSM attestation snippets.

I've started populating the owner roster and a short evidence index. Items I'm collecting first (examples):
- Identity & Access: OKTA SSO config export (primary), access roster CSV (fallback)
- Key Management: HSM usage notes + attestation (primary), KMS access logs (fallback)
- Runtime Telemetry: aggregated token-level latency/throughput metrics (primary), redacted request logs by day (fallback)

Attachments I'm pushing to the shared drive: owner-roster-template.csv, evidence-index-sample.docx. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRDW-CAIQ-playbook (restricted view — I'll add Zephyr viewers once we decide scope).

Note on redaction: for telemetry we will provide anonymized request-ids and non-PII metadata; payloads are out of scope. For chain-of-custody, we can include a signed cover letter from Security — please confirm if DocuSign is required.

Next steps for me: populate CSV with owners and retention windows, collect one redacted log export for your review, and drop a small sample HSM attestation (Karthik will attach). Expect an intermediary package by Monday morning PT.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Security Operations, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Soojin / Priyom —

This looks great, thank you. Confirming the following:
- Redacted session logs (timestamp + request-id + anonymized client id) are acceptable for telemetry samples.
- We do want a signed attestation for KMS/HSM claims; DocuSign is fine.

Priority controls (for our compliance bucket): IAM-01, KMS-02, RNT-05 (runtime telemetry), RMT-03 (runtime monitoring). I attached a short priority list so you can map first.

Please share the owner-roster CSV and a redacted telemetry sample by Monday morning PT and we'll begin our internal review. Once we see the sample artifacts, we'll confirm whether chain-of-custody needs to be formalized.

If needed, here's a good time for a short sync: Mon 07/05 09:00–09:30 PT.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

—Alex
